Cristyan Jiu-Jitsu & Fitness Earns Big Results at the Boston Fall International Open

November 10, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Cristyan Jiu-Jitsu & Fitness athletes delivered an impressive performance at the 2026 Boston Fall International Open, bringing home medals and valuable competition experience. The team competed across adult and kids divisions at this IBJJF tournament.

Adult Black Belt Results

Eduardo Pereira won gold in his weight division in both Gi and No-Gi. Along with Kosme Lima, he closed out the Gi and No-Gi Open Class divisions for Cristyan Jiu-Jitsu & Fitness.

Kosme Lima also earned gold in his weight division in both Gi and No-Gi, joining Eduardo to close out both Open Class divisions.

Edilton da Vitória won gold in the Gi weight division and Gi Open Class, as well as the No-Gi weight division. He also advanced to the quarterfinals in the No-Gi Open Class.

Jheniffer earned bronze in Gi.

Luiz Fernando reached the quarterfinals, and Maxwell won his exhibition match.

We’re proud of every athlete who stepped onto the mats and represented Cristyan Jiu-Jitsu & Fitness. The medals are a great achievement, and every match was an opportunity to learn, grow, and represent our team with heart.

Congratulations to all our competitors, coaches, and families who supported the team throughout the event!

What Is Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu? A Beginner's Guide for Hyannis Residents

October 21, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (BJJ) is a grappling martial art built around one simple idea: technique and leverage can beat size and strength. Instead of striking, you learn to control an opponent on the ground, escape bad positions, and finish with joint locks or chokes, always with a training partner who taps when they have had enough.

Where BJJ comes from

BJJ grew out of judo and traditional jiu-jitsu brought to Brazil in the early 1900s. Brazilian families refined it with a heavy focus on ground fighting, and it later became the foundation of modern mixed martial arts.

What a typical class looks like

Most classes start with a warm-up, move into drilling a specific technique with a partner, and finish with positional sparring or live rolling. Beginners are never thrown into the deep end. You learn the basics, such as how to fall safely, hold guard, and escape mount, before anything else.

Why so many people on Cape Cod are trying it

From Hyannis and Barnstable to Yarmouth and Mashpee, people are looking for workouts that are more engaging than a treadmill. BJJ gives you a full-body workout, practical self-defense, and a community of training partners in one place.

How to start

You don't need to be in shape or have any experience. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring water, and show up curious. At Cristyan Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Academy on Iyannough Rd in Hyannis, our coaches walk every new student through the fundamentals step by step.

Top 10 Benefits of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (For Body and Mind)

October 20, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

People walk into a jiu-jitsu academy for different reasons. Some want to get fit, some want to defend themselves, and some just want to try something new. Most of them stay for the benefits they didn't expect.

1. Full-body conditioning

Rolling works your grip, core, legs, and lungs all at once. It is strength and cardio training disguised as problem solving.

2. Practical self-defense

BJJ teaches you what to do if a fight hits the ground, which is where many real altercations end up.

3. Stress relief

It is hard to think about work emails while someone is trying to pass your guard. Training forces you into the present moment.

4. Confidence

Knowing you can stay calm under pressure carries over into job interviews, tough conversations, and everyday life.

5. Weight loss

An hour of class can burn a significant number of calories, and it is fun enough that you actually keep coming back.

6. Problem-solving skills

BJJ is often called human chess. Every position is a puzzle with many possible solutions.

7. Discipline and consistency

The belt system rewards showing up. Progress comes from steady effort, not shortcuts.

8. Better sleep

Hard training and lower stress add up to deeper, more restful sleep.

9. Community

Your training partners quickly become friends. Many students say their academy feels like a second family.

10. Lifelong learning

There is always another technique to learn, which keeps training interesting for decades.

Self-Defense

Is Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Good for Self-Defense?

October 16, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Many martial arts look impressive, but Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu stands out because it is tested every class against a resisting partner. That honesty is exactly what makes it effective for self-defense.

Real situations often end up on the ground

Scuffles frequently involve grabbing, clinching, and falling. BJJ teaches you how to stay safe from those positions, get back to your feet, or control someone until help arrives.

Size doesn't have to decide the outcome

BJJ was designed so a smaller person can use leverage, angles, and timing against a larger attacker. That makes it especially valuable for women, teens, and older adults.

You practice at full resistance

Live rolling lets you apply techniques against someone who is genuinely trying to stop you. You learn what works under pressure, not just in theory.

Calm under stress

Perhaps the biggest self-defense benefit is mental. After months of training, being pinned or grabbed no longer triggers panic, so you can think clearly.

Avoidance comes first

Good self-defense training also teaches awareness and de-escalation. The best fight is the one you never have.

What to Expect at Your First BJJ Class in Hyannis

October 12, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Walking into a martial arts academy for the first time can feel intimidating. Knowing what to expect makes it a lot easier.

Before class

Arrive 10 to 15 minutes early so you can meet the coach and fill out any paperwork. Let the instructor know it's your first time and mention any injuries.

What to wear

If you don't have a gi (the traditional uniform), wear a fitted t-shirt or rash guard and athletic shorts or leggings without zippers or pockets. Remove jewelry and trim your nails.

The warm-up

Expect light jogging, mobility work, and movements specific to jiu-jitsu like shrimping and bridging. Go at your own pace.

Technique instruction

The coach will demonstrate a technique, and you'll practice it with a partner. Experienced students are usually happy to help newcomers.

Sparring

Many academies let beginners watch or do light positional drills before live rolling. You will never be forced into anything you're not ready for.

After class

Drink water, ask questions, and expect to be a little sore the next day. That's normal.

Adult belts

Adults progress through white, blue, purple, brown, and black. Each belt also has stripes that mark progress along the way.

Kids belts

Children typically move through white, grey, yellow, orange, and green belts before they're old enough for the adult system.

Technical knowledge, the ability to apply techniques against resistance, attitude, and attendance all play a role.

The best advice for new students: don't chase belts. Show up, enjoy learning, and the promotions will come.

Gi vs. No-Gi Jiu-Jitsu: What's the Difference?

October 2, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu is practiced in two main styles: with the gi (a traditional kimono-style uniform) and without it, called no-gi.

Gi training

The gi gives you collars, sleeves, and pants to grip. That slows the game down, encourages precise technique, and opens up a huge range of chokes and sweeps.

No-gi training

No-gi is done in a rash guard and shorts. With fewer grips, it's faster and more scramble-heavy, and it translates closely to wrestling and MMA.

Which should beginners choose?

Many coaches suggest training both. The gi builds patience and technical detail, while no-gi sharpens speed and athleticism. Skills from one carry over to the other.

Self-defense considerations

In the real world, people wear clothes, so gi training is useful. But attackers might also wear t-shirts, so no-gi matters too.

Tell partners about injuries and ask them to go lighter when needed.

Sleep, hydration, and rest days are part of training.

7 Common Mistakes Beginners Make in Jiu-Jitsu

September 8, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Every black belt was once a beginner who made these mistakes. Knowing them ahead of time can save you frustration.

1. Using too much strength

Muscling through techniques burns you out fast. Focus on position and leverage.

2. Forgetting to breathe

Holding your breath drains your energy. Breathe slowly and steadily.

3. Not tapping early

Tap as soon as you're caught. It keeps you safe and training consistently.

4. Trying to learn everything at once

Focus on a few fundamentals instead of chasing flashy moves.

5. Comparing yourself to others

Everyone progresses at different speeds. Compare yourself to who you were last month.

6. Skipping fundamentals classes

The basics are what make advanced techniques work.

7. Quitting too soon

The first few months are the hardest. Push through and it gets much more rewarding.

What Is Capoeira? Brazil's Martial Art of Movement

September 4, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Capoeira is a Brazilian martial art with deep cultural roots, combining fluid movement, kicks, acrobatics, and live music.

History

Capoeira developed in Brazil among enslaved Africans and their descendants, who disguised fighting techniques as dance. Today it is recognized as an important part of Brazilian cultural heritage.

The roda

Capoeira is practiced in a circle called a roda, where two players move and interact to the rhythm of instruments like the berimbau.

Benefits

Capoeira builds flexibility, coordination, strength, and rhythm, and it is a joyful way to stay active.

A great complement to BJJ

The movement skills from capoeira improve balance and body control on the jiu-jitsu mats.

Shared roots

BJJ developed from judo techniques taught in Brazil in the early 20th century.

5 Jiu-Jitsu Fundamentals Every Beginner Should Learn

August 25, 2026 · Cristyan BJJ Academy, Hyannis MA

Advanced techniques are built on a handful of fundamentals. Master these and everything else gets easier.

1. The shrimp (hip escape)

This movement creates space and is the base of most escapes.

2. The bridge

Lifting your hips explosively helps you escape bottom positions like mount.

3. Closed guard

Holding an opponent between your legs is one of the first positions you'll learn, and one of the safest.

4. Posture and base

Staying balanced on top keeps you from getting swept.

5. Technical stand-up

Getting back to your feet safely is an essential self-defense skill.
